findings.description: ADR 0132 is already taken on `main` by `pup land --no-audit` (#240, at the merge base). This PR adds a second 0132, so every "decision 132" in the code now points at two decisions, and `adr-index.sh` has no check that would catch it.
findings.body:
**Duplicate decision number.** `docs/adr/0132-pup-land-no-audit-lets-several-lands-share-one.md` landed on `main` in #240 (`628cced`, already an ancestor of this PR's merge base) as decision 132. This PR adds `docs/adr/0132-a-gate-child-s-group-dies-with-pup-through-a.md` with the same number (line 1 `# 0132.`, line 6 `132.`). The regenerated index now lists two 0132 entries (`docs/adr/README.md` L154-155).

Rule (`docs/adr/README.md`): "The number is the decision's number, so every 'decision N' reference elsewhere stays valid." A new decision also takes "the highest `NNNN` on `origin/main` (after a fetch)" and increments it.

"Decision 132" is now ambiguous in both directions:
- `src/core/sandbox.utils.ts:203` (`(decision 132)`) and `src/core/sandbox-utils.test.ts:349` (`// Decision 132.`) mean the lifeline.
- `src/core/land.service.ts:45`, `src/core/types/land.types.ts:26`, `src/core/land.test.ts:330` and the link in `docs/adr/0084-…md:4` mean `--no-audit`.

`scripts/adr-index.sh` checks only that the index matches the files. It does not check that numbers are unique, so lint passes.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/94efd9b581de5f6c68de184826e5d2c971210f2a/docs/adr/0132-a-gate-child-s-group-dies-with-pup-through-a.md#L1-L6

**Fix:** renumber this ADR to 0133:
1. Rename the file and update its `# 0133.` title and `133.` entry.
2. Change `decision 132` / `Decision 132` to 133 at `src/core/sandbox.utils.ts:203` and `src/core/sandbox-utils.test.ts:349`.
3. Rerun `bash scripts/adr-index.sh`.

findings.description: The pup-killed test's generated script imports `join(process.cwd(), 'src', 'core', 'sandbox.utils.ts')`, so it breaks at runtime if the tests run from another cwd or the file moves. Resolving it with `new URL('./sandbox.utils.ts', import.meta.url)` removes the cwd dependency.

In the test comment "vitest stops a worker with SIGTERM, which pup forwards and gives a grace, then SIGKILLs it 500 ms later", the subject of "SIGKILLs it" reads as pup, but it is vitest that kills the worker. Rewording would make the sequence unambiguous.
